newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU publishes farm reform price cut proposals.
newsitem.headline: EU publishes farm reform price cut proposals.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday published proposals for further price cutting farm reforms that it says are needed to prepare for EU expansion eastwards and to prevent food surpluses returning.

The Agenda 2000 proposals, which were approved on Tuesday, include dairy, cereals and beef intervention price cuts of 10, 20 and 30 percent respectively and would be partially compensated by direct income payments.
The agriculture proposals, which were being presented by European Commission President Jacques Santer as part of a political, economic and financial package to the European Parliament, cover:
- 20 percent cut in cereals intervention price to 95.35 Ecus a tonne in 2000, from 119.19 in 1997

- A non-crop specific area payment for cereals, oilseeds and proteins of 66 Ecus a tonne multiplied by regional cereals reference yields set in the 1992 reform. The current rate for cereals is 54.35 Ecus.
The payment will be reduced if market prices remain at higher levels than foreseen.

- Reference rate for compulsory set-aside will be lowered to zero, from 17.5 percent. Voluntary set-aside will still be allowed but penalty set-aside abolished. Set-aside areas will receive the non-crop specific payment.
- Maize and other silage cereals will be excluded from the new regime.
- Supplementary aid of 13 Ecus a tonne will be paid for protein crops, such as peas and beans, to keep them competitive with cereals.
- Intervention price will be gradually lowered to 1,950 Ecus a tonne from 2,780 Ecus between 2000-2002.

- Direct income payments would be gradually increased with the yearly suckler cow premium rising to 215 Ecus per head from 145, the single bull payment rising to 368 from 135 and a new dairy cow yearly payment of 70 Ecus per head.
- Quotas extended to 2006 at their current levels - Intervention prices gradually reduced by 10 percent to 2006.
